title.zh: 卷九十三 列傳第十八 李靖孫:令問 五代孫:彥芳 李勣孫:敬業
title.en: Volume 93 Biographies 18: Li Jing and Grandson: Ling Wen, Wu Dai and Grandson: Yan Fang, Li Ji and Grandson: Jing Ye
title.raw: 卷九十三 列傳第十八 李靖孫:令問 五代孫:彥芳 李勣孫:敬業 Volume 93 Biographies 18: Li Jing and Grandson: Ling Wen, Wu Dai and Grandson: Yan Fang, Li Ji and Grandson: Jing Ye

sentences.zh: 李靖弟:客師 孫:令問 五代孫:彥芳 李勣孫:敬業

translations.literal: Li Jing's brother: Keshe; grandson: Lingwen; fifth-generation grandson: Yanfang; Li Ji's grandson: Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing — brother: Keshe; grandson: Lingwen; fifth-generation descendant: Yanfang; Li Ji — grandson: Jingye.

sentences.zh: 李靖，字藥師，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Li Jing, styled Yaoshi, was a man of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, whose style name was Yaoshi, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 姿貌魁秀，通書史。

translations.literal: His bearing was tall and handsome; he was versed in books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and striking in appearance, he was well read in the classics and history.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「丈夫遭遇，要當以功名取富貴，何至作章句儒！」

translations.literal: He once said to those close to him: "When a man meets his opportunity, he ought to win wealth and rank through achievement and fame—why become a pedant of textual learning!"
translations.idiomatic: He once told those close to him, "When a man finds his moment, he should win wealth and standing through deeds and renown—why settle for being a bookish scholar of classical lines?"

sentences.zh: 其舅韓擒虎每與論兵，輒歎曰：「可與語孫、吳者，非斯人尚誰哉！」

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Han Qinhu, whenever he discussed warfare with him, would sigh and say: "One with whom one can speak of Sunzi and Wuzi—if not this man, then who?"
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Han Qinhu, whenever they talked of war, would sigh and say, "If there is anyone worth discussing Sunzi and Wuzi with, who else could it be but this man?"

sentences.zh: 仕隋為殿內直長，吏部尚書牛弘見之曰：「王佐才也！」

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Director of Palace Attendants; the Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, on meeting him, said: "Talent fit to assist a king!"
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as a director in the palace service. Niu Hong, Minister of Personnel, met him and declared, "Here is talent fit to assist a sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 左僕射楊素拊其床謂曰：「卿終當坐此！」

translations.literal: The Left Vice Premier Yang Su, patting his own couch, told him: "You will end by sitting in this place!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, Left Vice Premier, slapped his own seat and told him, "You will one day sit in this very chair!"

sentences.zh: 大業末，為馬邑丞。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, he was magistrate of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Yang's Daye era, he served as magistrate of Mayi.

sentences.zh: 高祖擊突厥，靖察有非常志，自囚上急變，傳送江都，至長安，道梗。

translations.literal: When Gaozu attacked the Turks, Jing perceived his extraordinary intent, imprisoned himself, and reported an urgent change of circumstances to be sent to Jiangdu; he reached Chang'an, but the roads were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu struck the Turks, Jing sensed his exceptional ambition, had himself bound, and sent word of an urgent crisis to be forwarded to Jiangdu; he reached Chang'an, but the routes were cut.

sentences.zh: 高祖已定京師，將斬之，靖呼曰：「公起兵為天下除暴亂，欲就大事，以私怨殺誼士乎？」

translations.literal: After Gaozu had secured the capital, he was about to execute him; Jing cried out: "Your Lordship raised troops to remove violence and disorder from the realm and wish to accomplish the great enterprise—will you kill a man of principle over a private grudge?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu held the capital, he was about to put Jing to death. Jing called out, "You took up arms to purge the realm of violence and chaos and mean to finish the great work—will you kill a man of principle over a private grievance?"

sentences.zh: 秦王亦為請，得釋，引為三衛。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin also pleaded for him; he was released and appointed to the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin pleaded as well; Jing was spared and brought into the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 從平王世充，以功授開府。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Wang Shichong and, for merit, was granted an Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign that pacified Wang Shichong and, for his service, received an Opening Office commission.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑據江陵，詔靖安輯，從數輕騎道金州，會蠻賊鄧世洛兵數萬屯山谷間，廬江王瑗討不勝，靖為瑗謀，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Xiao Xun held Jiangling; an edict ordered Jing to pacify the region. With a few light horsemen he took the route through Jinzhou, encountered the barbarian bandit Deng Shiluo with tens of thousands of troops encamped in the mountain valleys; the Prince of Lujiang Yuan could not defeat him, but Jing devised a plan for Yuan and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xun held Jiangling, and Jing was ordered to pacify the region. He rode ahead with a handful of light cavalry by way of Jinzhou, ran into the rebel Deng Shiluo and tens of thousands of men camped in the valleys, and when Prince Yuan of Lujiang could not prevail, Jing planned the attack for him and beat the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 進至峽州，阻銑兵不得前。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xiazhou, he was blocked by Xun's troops and could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Xiazhou but was held up by Xun's forces and could not move forward.

sentences.zh: 帝謂逗留，詔都督許紹斬靖，紹為請而免。

translations.literal: The emperor judged him to be lingering; an edict ordered the Area Commander Xu Shao to execute Jing; Shao pleaded on his behalf and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this for delay; an edict told Area Commander Xu Shao to behead Jing, but Shao interceded and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 開州蠻冉肇則寇夔州，趙郡王孝恭戰未利，靖率兵八百破其屯，要險設伏，斬肇則，俘禽五千。

translations.literal: The Kaizhou barbarian Ran Zhaoze raided Kuizhou; the Prince of Zhao Jun Xiaogong's battle went ill; Jing led eight hundred men, smashed their encampment, seized a defile to set an ambush, beheaded Zhaoze, and captured five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zhaoze of the Kaizhou tribes raided Kuizhou; Prince Xiaogong of Zhao command fought without success until Jing led eight hundred men, broke their camp, took a choke point for an ambush, killed Zhaoze, and took five thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「使功不如使過，靖果然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to those beside him: "To employ merit is not as good as to employ fault—Jing is indeed so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants, "Using a man's fault works better than using his merit—and Jing proves it."

sentences.zh: 因手敕勞曰：「既往不咎，向事吾久已忘之。」

translations.literal: He then wrote a personal edict of encouragement, saying: "The past is not to be blamed; what went before I have long since forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: He followed with a personal edict of praise: "What is past is not held against you; I have long since forgotten the earlier affair."

sentences.zh: 靖遂陳圖銑十策。

translations.literal: Jing then presented ten stratagems for dealing with Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then laid out ten plans for subduing Xiao Xun.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜靖行軍總管，兼攝孝恭行軍長史，軍政一委焉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jing Campaign Commander-in-Chief and, concurrently, acting Chief of Staff on Xiaogong's campaign staff; military and civil affairs were wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Jing Campaign Commander-in-Chief and acting chief of staff on Xiaogong's staff, with full charge of military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 武德四年八月，大閱兵夔州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Wude, he held a grand review of troops at Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Wude 4, he held a grand troop review at Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 時秋潦，濤瀨漲惡，銑以靖未能下，不設備。

translations.literal: It was the season of autumn floods; the rapids and shallows swelled dangerously; Xun thought Jing could not descend and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn floods had swollen the currents and shoals; Xun assumed Jing could not come downriver and left his defenses slack.

sentences.zh: 諸將亦請江平乃進。

translations.literal: The generals also asked to wait until the river was calm before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals too urged waiting until the river subsided before advancing.

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「兵機事，以速為神。

translations.literal: Jing said: "In military opportunity, speed is divine.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "In war, timing is everything—and speed is its soul.

sentences.zh: 今士始集，銑不及知，若乘水傅壘，是震霆不及塞耳，有能倉卒召兵，無以禦我，此必禽也。」

translations.literal: Now the troops have only just assembled; Xun cannot know in time—if we ride the water to assault their ramparts, it is like thunder before one can stop one's ears; even if they could hastily summon soldiers, they could not resist us—this prey is sure to be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Our men have only just gathered; Xun cannot know in time. If we ride the flood to strike their walls, it will be like thunder before anyone can cover his ears. Even a hurried call-up could not stop us—he is ours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 孝恭從之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 九月，舟師叩夷陵，銑將文士弘以卒數萬屯清江，孝恭欲擊之，靖曰：「不可。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the fleet struck Yiling; Xun's general Wen Shihong encamped on the Qing River with tens of thousands of men; Xiaogong wished to attack; Jing said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the fleet reached Yiling. Xun's general Wen Shihong held the Qing River with tens of thousands of men. Xiaogong wanted to attack at once, but Jing said, "No.

sentences.zh: 士弘健將，下皆勇士，今新失荊門，悉銳拒我，此救敗之師，不可當。

translations.literal: Shihong is a vigorous commander and his men are all warriors; having just lost Jingmen, they will throw their full strength against us—this is an army fighting to redeem defeat and cannot be faced.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong is a strong commander and his troops are all seasoned fighters. Fresh from the loss of Jingmen, they will meet us with everything they have—an army fighting to redeem a defeat, and not to be met head-on.

sentences.zh: 宜駐南岸，待其氣衰乃取之。」

translations.literal: We ought to hold the south bank and wait until their spirit declines before taking them."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the south bank and wait until their ardor fades, then take them."

sentences.zh: 孝恭不聽，留靖守屯，自往與戰，大敗還。

translations.literal: Xiaogong would not listen, left Jing to guard the camp, went himself to give battle, and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong refused to listen, left Jing to hold the camp, went to fight himself, and came back in rout.

sentences.zh: 賊委舟散掠，靖視其亂，縱兵擊破之，取四百餘艘，溺死者萬人。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned their boats and scattered to plunder; Jing saw their disorder and loosed his troops to smash them, taking more than four hundred vessels; ten thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy abandoned their boats and scattered to loot. Jing saw the disorder, sent his men in, and broke them, seizing more than four hundred craft while ten thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 即率輕兵五千為先鋒，趨江陵，薄城而營。

translations.literal: He then led five thousand light troops as vanguard, hurried to Jiangling, and pitched camp close to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He at once led five thousand light troops as vanguard, raced to Jiangling, and camped under the walls.

sentences.zh: 破其將楊君茂、鄭文秀，俘甲士四千。

translations.literal: He defeated their generals Yang Junmao and Zheng Wenxiu and captured four thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Xun's generals Yang Junmao and Zheng Wenxiu and took four thousand armored men prisoner.

sentences.zh: 孝恭軍繼進，銑大懼，檄召江南兵，不及到，明日降。

translations.literal: Xiaogong's army followed up; Xun was greatly afraid, issued urgent summons for Jiangnan troops, but they could not arrive in time; the next day he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong's main force came up. Xun was terrified, called the Jiangnan armies by urgent dispatch, but they could not arrive in time, and he surrendered the next day.

sentences.zh: 靖入其都，號令靜嚴，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: Jing entered the rebel capital; his orders were calm and strict, and the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Jing entered the rebel capital. His orders were calm and strict, and the army took no private plunder.

sentences.zh: 或請靖籍銑將拒戰者家貲以賞軍，靖曰：「王者之兵，弔人而取有罪，彼其脅驅以來，藉以拒師，本非所情，不容以叛逆比之。

translations.literal: Some asked Jing to register the household property of Xun's generals who had resisted and use it to reward the army; Jing said: "The army of a true king succors the people and takes only the guilty; those men were driven under compulsion to come and used that excuse to resist our forces—they were not rebels at heart and must not be treated as such.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Jing to seize the estates of Xun's commanders who had fought on and use them to reward the troops. Jing said, "A king's army succors the people and punishes only the guilty. Those men were pressed into service and fought because they had to—not because they chose rebellion—and must not be treated as traitors.

sentences.zh: 今新定荊、郢，宜示寬大，以慰其心，若降而籍之，恐自荊而南，堅城劇屯，驅之死守，非計之善也。」

translations.literal: Jing and Ying have only just been pacified; we should show magnanimity to reassure their hearts—if we register property after surrender, I fear that from Jing southward every strong city and major garrison will be driven to die in defense; that is not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Ying have only just been secured; we should show mercy to reassure them. If we seize property from men who surrender, every stronghold south of Jing may be driven to fight to the death—not sound policy."

sentences.zh: 止不籍。

translations.literal: He stopped and did not register their property.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade any such registration.

sentences.zh: 由是江、漢列城爭下。

translations.literal: Because of this the walled cities along the Yangzi and Han submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the cities along the Yangzi and Han submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 以功封永康縣公，檢校荊州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongkang County and made Acting Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yongkang and named acting governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃度嶺至桂州，分道招慰。

translations.literal: He then crossed the ranges to Guizhou and sent parties on separate routes to offer reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the mountains into Guizhou and sent detachments on separate routes to win submission.

sentences.zh: 酋領馮盎等皆以子弟來謁，南方悉定。

translations.literal: Tribal leaders such as Feng Ang all came to pay court with sons and younger brothers; the south was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains such as Feng Ang came in person with sons and younger kin to pay homage, and the south was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 裁量款效，承制補官。

translations.literal: He weighed degrees of submission and, by imperial commission, filled official posts.
translations.idiomatic: He judged each group's degree of loyalty and, under imperial authority, appointed officials accordingly.

sentences.zh: 得郡凡九十六，戶六十余萬。

translations.literal: He gained ninety-six commanderies in all, with more than six hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety-six commanderies came in, with more than six hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詔書勞勉，授嶺南撫慰大使、檢校桂州總管。

translations.literal: An edict praised and encouraged him; he was appointed Commissioner to Pacify Lingnan and Acting Area Commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his work and named him Commissioner to Pacify Lingnan and acting area commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 以嶺海陋遠，久不見德，非震威武、示禮義，則無以變風。

translations.literal: Because the Lingnan coast was remote and backward and had long gone without imperial grace, unless awe-inspiring might and ritual propriety were displayed, there was no way to change their customs.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingnan coast was remote and had long gone without imperial favor; without a show of might and of ritual propriety, there was no changing local ways.

sentences.zh: 即率兵南巡，所過問疾苦，延見長老，宣佈天子恩意，遠近歡服。

translations.literal: He at once led troops on a southern tour; wherever he passed he inquired into hardships, received elders, and proclaimed the Son of Heaven's gracious intent; near and far rejoiced and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops south on tour, inquiring into hardships wherever he went, receiving local elders, and proclaiming the emperor's grace; near and far, all submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏據丹陽反，詔孝恭為帥，召靖入朝受方略，副孝恭東討，李世勣等七總管皆受節度。

translations.literal: Fu Gongshi held Danyang in rebellion; an edict made Xiaogong commander; Jing was summoned to court to receive strategy, served as Xiaogong's deputy in the eastern campaign, and the seven area commanders including Li Shiji all came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi rebelled from Danyang. Xiaogong was named supreme commander; Jing was called to court for the plan, made Xiaogong's deputy in the eastern campaign, and seven area commanders including Li Shiji were placed under his direction.

sentences.zh: 公祏遣馮惠亮以舟師三萬屯當塗，陳正通步騎二萬屯青林，自梁山連鎖以斷江道。

translations.literal: Gongshi sent Feng Huiliang with thirty thousand naval troops to encamp at Dangtu, Chen Zhengtong with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry at Qinglin, and from Liangshan chained the river to cut the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi sent Feng Huiliang with thirty thousand sailors to hold Dangtu and Chen Zhengtong with twenty thousand foot and horse to hold Qinglin, while from Liangshan they chained the river to block the waterway.

sentences.zh: 築卻月城，延袤十餘里，為犄角。

translations.literal: They built the Crescent Fort, extending more than ten li, as a horn position.
translations.idiomatic: They built the Crescent Fort, stretching more than ten li, as a supporting bastion.

sentences.zh: 諸將議曰：「彼勁兵連柵，將不戰疲老我師。

translations.literal: The generals deliberated, saying: "Their strong troops are chained in palisades; they intend not to fight but to weary and age our army.
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued, "Their best men are behind chained palisades—they mean to avoid battle and wear our army down.

sentences.zh: 若直取丹陽，空其巢窟，惠亮等自降。」

translations.literal: If we strike straight for Danyang and empty their nest, Huiliang and the rest will surrender of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Strike straight for Danyang and empty their lair, and Huiliang and the rest will yield on their own."

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Jing said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "No.

sentences.zh: 二軍雖精，而公祏所自將亦銳卒也，既保石頭，則牢未可拔。

translations.literal: Though those two armies are elite, the troops Gongshi leads in person are also sharp soldiers; once he holds Shitou, the stronghold cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Those two armies are strong, but Gongshi's personal force is elite too. Once he holds Shitou, the fortress cannot be cracked.

sentences.zh: 我留不得志，退有所忌，腹背蒙患，非百全計。

translations.literal: If we stay we gain nothing; if we withdraw we have fears behind us—trouble on belly and back is not a plan of full security.
translations.idiomatic: If we linger we accomplish nothing; if we withdraw we expose our rear. Trouble on both flanks is no sure plan.

sentences.zh: 且惠亮、正通百戰餘賊，非怯野鬥，今方持重，特公祏立計爾。

translations.literal: Moreover Huiliang and Zhengtong are battle-hardened remnants, not men who shrink from field fighting; they are being cautious now only because Gongshi has laid down the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Huiliang and Zhengtong are veterans, not men afraid of open battle. They hold back now only because Gongshi has set the plan.

sentences.zh: 若出不意，挑攻其城，必破之。

translations.literal: If we take them unawares and provoke an attack on their fort, it is sure to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Take them by surprise and strike their fort—they will break.

sentences.zh: 惠亮拔，公祏禽矣。」

translations.literal: Once Huiliang is uprooted, Gongshi can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Uproot Huiliang, and Gongshi is ours."

sentences.zh: 孝恭聽之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong agreed.

sentences.zh: 靖率黃君漢等水陸皆進，苦戰，殺傷萬余人，惠亮等亡去。

translations.literal: Jing led Huang Junhan and others, advancing by land and water alike; after bitter fighting more than ten thousand were killed or wounded; Huiliang and the rest fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led Huang Junhan and others forward by land and water, fought bitterly, killed or wounded more than ten thousand, and drove Huiliang and his men off.

sentences.zh: 靖將輕兵至丹陽，公祏懼，眾尚多，不能戰，乃出走，禽之，江南平。

translations.literal: Jing led light troops to Danyang; Gongshi was afraid; though his forces were still numerous he could not fight and fled; he was captured and Jiangnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jing took light troops to Danyang. Gongshi was afraid; though his men were still many, he could not fight and fled. He was captured, and Jiangnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 置東南道行台，以為行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The Southeast Circuit Executive Agency was established; he was made its Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: A Southeast Circuit executive agency was set up, and he was made its Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 賜物千段、奴婢百口、馬百匹。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand bolts of goods, a hundred slaves, and a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He received a thousand bolts of goods, a hundred slaves, and a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 行台廢，檢校揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: When the executive agency was abolished, he became Acting Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: When the executive agency was abolished, he became acting chief administrator of the Yangzhou superior command.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「靖乃銑、公祏之膏肓也，古韓、白、衛、霍何以加！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "Jing is the deep-seated malady of Xun and Gongshi—how could the ancient Han Xin, Bai Qi, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing surpass him!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "Jing was the fatal sickness of Xiao Xun and Fu Gongshi—what could the ancient Han Xin, Bai Qi, Wei Qing, or Huo Qubing add to that?"

sentences.zh: 八年，突厥寇太原，為行軍總管，以江淮兵萬人屯太谷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Turks raided Taiyuan; he was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief and stationed ten thousand Jiang-Huai troops at Taigu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Turks raided Taiyuan, he was made campaign commander and posted ten thousand Jiang-Huai troops at Taigu.

sentences.zh: 時諸將多敗，獨靖以完軍歸。

translations.literal: At that time most generals were defeated; only Jing returned with his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Most commanders were defeated; only Jing brought his army back whole.

sentences.zh: 俄權檢校安州大都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Superior Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named acting superior governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐阼，授刑部尚書，錄功，賜實封四百戶，兼檢校中書令。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, he was appointed Minister of Justice, entered merit rolls, granted four hundred taxable households in substantive enfeoffment, and concurrently made Acting Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Jing became Minister of Justice, was entered on the merit rolls, received four hundred taxable households in substantive enfeoffment, and was also named acting director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 突厥部種離畔，帝方圖進取，以兵部尚書為定襄道行軍總管，率勁騎三千繇馬邑趨惡陽嶺。

translations.literal: Turkic tribes were splitting away; the emperor was planning an advance; as Minister of War he was made Campaign Commander of the Dingxiang Circuit, leading three thousand crack cavalry from Mayi toward the Wuyang Range.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic tribes were breaking away, and the emperor planned an advance. As Minister of War, Jing was made campaign commander on the Dingxiang circuit and led three thousand elite horsemen from Mayi toward the Wuyang Range.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗大驚，曰：「兵不傾國來，靖敢提孤軍至此？」

translations.literal: Jieli Khan was greatly alarmed and said: "If troops do not come with the full strength of the state, how dare Jing bring a lone army here?"
translations.idiomatic: Jieli Khan was stunned. "If they did not send the whole empire's army," he said, "how dare Jing bring a lone force this far?"

sentences.zh: 於是帳部數恐。

translations.literal: At this the yurt clans were many times afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At that, fear spread through the camp clans.

sentences.zh: 靖縱諜者離其腹心，夜襲定襄，破之，可汗脫身遁磧口。

translations.literal: Jing set spies loose to sunder their inner circle, raided Dingxiang by night, broke them, and the khan escaped alone to the desert pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent agents to split their inner circle, struck Dingxiang by night, broke them, and the khan fled alone toward the desert pass.

sentences.zh: 進封代國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「李陵以步卒五千絕漠，然卒降匈奴，其功尚得書竹帛。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Li Ling with five thousand foot soldiers crossed the desert, yet in the end surrendered to the Xiongnu—still his achievement was written on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Li Ling took five thousand foot soldiers across the desert, yet in the end surrendered to the Xiongnu—and still his deed was written into the histories.

sentences.zh: 靖以騎三千，蹀血虜庭，遂取定襄，古未有輩，足澡吾渭水之恥矣！」

translations.literal: Jing with three thousand horsemen trampled blood in the barbarian court and took Dingxiang—there has been no like in antiquity; it is enough to wash away my shame at the Wei River!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing with three thousand horsemen trampled the enemy court in blood and took Dingxiang—unmatched since antiquity—enough to wash away my shame at the Wei River!"

sentences.zh: 頡利走保鐵山，遣使者謝罪，請舉國內附。

translations.literal: Jieli fled to hold Tieshan, sent envoys to apologize for his crimes, and asked to submit the whole nation.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli withdrew to Tieshan, sent envoys to apologize, and asked to bring the whole nation under Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 以靖為定襄道總管往迎之。

translations.literal: Jing was made Area Commander of the Dingxiang Circuit to go welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was made area commander on the Dingxiang circuit to go receive him.

sentences.zh: 又遣鴻臚卿唐儉、將軍安修仁慰撫。

translations.literal: The Court also sent the Director of Guests Tang Jian and General An Xiuren to console and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent Director of Guests Tang Jian and General An Xiuren to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 靖謂副將張公謹曰：「詔使到，虜必自安，若萬騎齎二十日糧，自白道襲之，必得所欲。」

translations.literal: Jing told his deputy Zhang Gongjin: "When the imperial envoy arrives the barbarians will surely feel secure; if ten thousand horsemen carry twenty days' rations and strike by the White Route, we are sure to gain what we desire."
translations.idiomatic: Jing told his deputy Zhang Gongjin, "Once the imperial envoy arrives, the Turks will relax. Ten thousand horsemen with twenty days' rations, striking by the White Route—we will get what we want."

sentences.zh: 公謹曰：「上已與約降，行人在彼，奈何？」

translations.literal: Gongjin said: "The sovereign has already agreed to accept their surrender; our envoys are there—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongjin said, "The emperor has already agreed to their surrender. Our envoys are there—what then?"

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「機不可失，韓信所以破齊也。

translations.literal: Jing said: "Opportunity must not be lost—that is how Han Xin broke Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Opportunity cannot be lost—that is how Han Xin broke Qi.

sentences.zh: 如唐儉輩何足惜哉！」

translations.literal: Men like Tang Jian—what are they worth regretting!"
translations.idiomatic: What is a man like Tang Jian worth regretting?"

sentences.zh: 督兵疾進，行遇候邏，皆俘以從，去其牙七里乃覺，部眾震潰，斬萬餘級，俘男女十萬，禽其子疊羅施，殺義成公主。

translations.literal: He drove the army forward at speed; on the march they met scouts and took them all along; seven li from the royal camp the enemy only then realized; the tribes shook apart and collapsed; more than ten thousand were beheaded; a hundred thousand men and women were captured; his son Die Luoshi was taken; Princess Yicheng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the army forward fast. Every scout they met was taken along. Seven li from the royal camp the enemy realized what was happening; the tribes broke and fled. More than ten thousand were killed, a hundred thousand men and women captured, Jieli's son Die Luoshi taken, and Princess Yicheng killed.

sentences.zh: 頡利亡去，為大同道行軍總管張寶相禽以獻。

translations.literal: Jieli fled and was captured and presented by Zhang Baoxiang, Campaign Commander of the Datong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli fled and was captured and presented by Zhang Baoxiang, campaign commander on the Datong circuit.

sentences.zh: 於是斥地自陰山北至大漠矣。

translations.literal: Thus the frontier was pushed from the Yin Mountains northward to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier now ran from the Yin Mountains north to the great desert.

sentences.zh: 帝因大赦天下，賜民五日酺。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon proclaimed a great amnesty for the realm and granted the people five days of public feasting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and granted the people five days of public celebration.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫蕭瑀劾靖持軍無律，縱士大掠，散失奇寶。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xiao Yu impeached Jing for holding the army without discipline, letting the soldiers plunder greatly, and scattering and losing rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xiao Yu accused Jing of lax discipline, allowing great plunder, and the loss of rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 帝召讓之，靖無所辯，頓首謝。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and reproached him; Jing had nothing to argue and kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned and rebuked him. Jing offered no defense and kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 帝徐曰：「隋史萬歲破達頭可汗，不賞而誅，朕不然，赦公之罪，錄公之功。」

translations.literal: The emperor said slowly: "In the Sui, Shi Wansui defeated Khan Datou and was not rewarded but executed—I am not like that; I pardon your offense and record your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said slowly, "Under the Sui, Shi Wansui defeated Khan Datou and was not rewarded but executed. I am not like that. I pardon your fault and record your merit."

sentences.zh: 乃進左光祿大夫，賜絹千匹，增戶至五百。

translations.literal: He was then advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted a thousand bolts of silk, and his households increased to five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, given a thousand bolts of silk, and his enfeoffment raised to five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「向人譖短公，朕今悟矣。」

translations.literal: He then said: "Someone before slandered you—I understand now."
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "Someone slandered you before—I see it now."

sentences.zh: 加賜帛一千匹，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He added a grant of another thousand bolts of silk and transferred him to Right Vice Premier of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He added another thousand bolts of silk and made him Right Vice Premier.

sentences.zh: 靖每參議，恂恂似不能言，以沈厚稱。

translations.literal: Whenever Jing took part in deliberation he was deferential, as if unable to speak, and was praised for depth and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: In council Jing was deferential, almost as if he could not speak, and was praised for depth and steadiness.

sentences.zh: 時遣使十六道巡察風俗，以靖為畿內道大使，會足疾，懇乞骸骨。

translations.literal: At that time envoys were sent on sixteen circuits to inspect local customs; Jing was made envoy for the Metropolitan Circuit; he happened to suffer foot ailment and earnestly begged to retire his bones.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were then sent on sixteen circuits to inspect local customs, and Jing was named envoy for the metropolitan circuit. When foot ailment struck, he earnestly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中書侍郎岑文本諭旨曰：「自古富貴而知止者蓋少，雖疾頓憊，猶力於進。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Secretariat Vice Director Cen Wende to convey his intent, saying: "From antiquity those who knew when to stop amid wealth and rank have been few; though ill and utterly weary, they still strive to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Secretariat Vice Director Cen Wende with his message: "Since antiquity, few who have known wealth and rank have also known when to stop. Though ill and worn out, most still push on.

sentences.zh: 公今引大體，朕深嘉之。

translations.literal: You now invoke the larger principle—I deeply commend it.
translations.idiomatic: You now appeal to the larger principle, and I deeply commend it.

sentences.zh: 欲成公美，為一代法，不可不聽。」

translations.literal: I wish to complete your excellence and make you a model for a generation—I cannot but grant this."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to complete your honor and make you a model for the age—I cannot refuse."

sentences.zh: 乃授檢校特進，就第，賜物段千，尚乘馬二，祿賜、國官、府佐皆勿廢。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Acting Special Advancement, to dwell at his estate, granted a thousand bolts of goods and two imperial riding horses; salary, gifts, household officials, and estate staff were all left unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was named acting Special Advancement and sent to his estate, with a thousand bolts of goods and two imperial riding horses; salary, gifts, household staff, and estate officers were all left in place.

sentences.zh: 若疾少間，三日一至門下中書平章政事。

translations.literal: If the illness eased somewhat, he was to come once every three days to the Secretariat and Chancellery to deliberate on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: If his illness eased, he was to attend the Secretariat and Chancellery every third day to deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 加賜靈壽杖。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted a staff of lingzhi wood.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given a lingzhi staff.

sentences.zh: 頃之，吐谷渾寇邊。

translations.literal: Before long the Tuyuhun raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tuyuhun raided the border.

sentences.zh: 帝謂侍臣曰：「靖能復起為帥乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "Can Jing rise again to serve as commander?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his attendants, "Can Jing take the field again as commander?"

sentences.zh: 靖往見房玄齡，曰：「吾雖老，尚堪一行。」

translations.literal: Jing went to see Fang Xuanling and said: "Though I am old, I can still manage one campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Jing went to Fang Xuanling and said, "I am old, but I can still manage one campaign."

sentences.zh: 帝喜，以為西海道行軍大總管，任城王道宗、侯君集、李大亮、李道彥、高甑生五總管兵皆屬。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and made him Grand Campaign Commander of the Xihai Circuit; the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong, Hou Junji, Li Daliang, Li Daoyan, and Gao Zaosheng—the troops of all five area commanders—were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and named him grand campaign commander on the Xihai circuit. The Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong, Hou Junji, Li Daliang, Li Daoyan, and Gao Zaosheng—all five area commanders and their troops—were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 軍次伏俟城，吐谷渾盡火其莽，退保大非川。

translations.literal: The army halted at Fuxi City; the Tuyuhun burned all their pasturelands and withdrew to hold the Dafei River.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Fuxi City. The Tuyuhun burned their pasturelands and withdrew to the Dafei River.

sentences.zh: 諸將議，春草未芽，馬弱不可戰。

translations.literal: The generals deliberated: spring grass had not yet sprouted and the horses were weak—they could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued that spring grass had not yet sprouted and the horses were too weak to fight.

sentences.zh: 靖決策深入，遂逾積石山。

translations.literal: Jing decided on a deep advance and crossed the Jishi Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Jing decided to push deep inland and crossed the Jishi Mountains.

sentences.zh: 大戰數十，多所殺獲，殘其國，國人多降，吐谷渾伏允愁蹙自經死。

translations.literal: Great battles were fought dozens of times; many were killed or captured; their state was shattered; many of their people surrendered; the Tuyuhun ruler Fuyun, in anguish, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of major engagements, with heavy kills and captures, their state was broken. Many submitted. The Tuyuhun ruler Fuyun, in despair, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 靖更立大寧王慕容順而還。

translations.literal: Jing installed the Prince of Daning Murong Shun and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jing installed the Prince of Daning Murong Shun as ruler and returned.

sentences.zh: 甑生軍繇鹽澤道後期，靖簿責之。

translations.literal: Zaosheng's army, taking the Salt Marsh route, was late; Jing entered it in the register and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zaosheng's column, on the Salt Marsh route, arrived late. Jing recorded the fault and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 既歸而憾，與廣州長史唐奉義告靖謀反，有司按驗無狀，甑生等以誣罔論。

translations.literal: After returning he bore resentment and, with Tang Fengyi, Chief Administrator of Guangzhou, accused Jing of plotting rebellion; the authorities investigated and found no substance; Zaosheng and others were judged for false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he nursed a grudge and, with Guangzhou chief administrator Tang Fengyi, accused Jing of treason. The investigation found nothing. Zaosheng and his allies were punished for false accusation.

sentences.zh: 靖乃闔門自守，賓客親戚一謝遣。

translations.literal: Jing then shut his gates and kept to himself, dismissing all guests and kin with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Jing shut his gates and kept to himself, politely dismissing every guest and kinsman.

sentences.zh: 改衛國公。

translations.literal: His title was changed to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 其妻卒，詔墳制如衛、霍故事，築闕象鐵山、積石山，以旌其功，進開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When his wife died, an edict ordered tomb arrangements after the precedents of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, building gate-towers modeled on Tieshan and the Jishi Mountains to honor his achievements; he was advanced to Opening Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife died, an edict ordered a tomb like those of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, with gate-towers shaped like Tieshan and the Jishi Mountains to honor his deeds. He was promoted to Opening Office with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐遼，召靖入，謂曰：「公南平吳，北破突厥，西定吐谷渾，惟高麗未服，亦有意乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to campaign against Liaodong and summoned Jing, saying: "You pacified Wu in the south, broke the Turks in the north, and settled the Tuyuhun in the west—only Goguryeo is not yet subdued; do you have the will for this too?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to campaign against Liaodong, he summoned Jing and said, "You pacified Wu in the south, broke the Turks in the north, and settled the Tuyuhun in the west. Only Goguryeo remains. Are you willing?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「往憑天威，得效尺寸功。

translations.literal: He replied: "In the past I relied on Heaven's majesty and was able to render a modicum of service.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In the past I relied on your majesty and was able to do a little.

sentences.zh: 今疾雖衰，陛下誠不棄，病且瘳矣。」

translations.literal: Though my illness has weakened me, if Your Majesty truly does not cast me aside, the sickness will yet recover."
translations.idiomatic: My illness has weakened me, but if Your Majesty will not cast me aside, I may yet recover."

sentences.zh: 帝憫其老，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied his age and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied his age and refused.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，病甚，帝幸其第，流涕曰：「公乃朕生平故人，于國有勞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his illness was severe; the emperor visited his residence and, weeping, said: "You are an old friend of my whole life and have toiled for the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year his illness grew grave. The emperor visited his home and wept, saying, "You are a friend of my whole life, and you have served the state long and well.

sentences.zh: 今疾若此，為公憂之。」

translations.literal: Now that your illness is thus, I grieve for you."
translations.idiomatic: To see you so ill grieves me."

sentences.zh: 薨，年七十九，贈司徒、并州都督，給班劍、羽葆、鼓吹，陪葬昭陵，諡日景武。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-nine; posthumously made Minister of Education and Area Commander of Bingzhou; granted court swords, feathered parasols, and martial music; buried beside Zhaoling; posthumous title Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine. He was posthumously made Minister of Education and area commander of Bingzhou, granted court swords, feathered parasols, and martial music, buried beside Zhaoling, and given the posthumous title Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 子德謇嗣，官至將作少匠，坐善太子承乾，流嶺南，以靖故徙吳郡。

translations.literal: His son Deqian succeeded; rose to Assistant Director of Palace Construction; punished for befriending Crown Prince Chengan, exiled to Lingnan, and because of Jing moved to Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deqian succeeded him, rose to assistant director of palace construction, was punished for befriending Crown Prince Chengan and exiled to Lingnan, then moved to Wu commandery on account of Jing.

sentences.zh: 靖兄端，字藥王，以靖功襲永康公，梓州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing's elder brother Duan, styled Yaowang, inherited the title Duke of Yongkang through Jing's merit and served as Governor of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's elder brother Duan, styled Yaowang, inherited the title Duke of Yongkang through Jing's merit and served as governor of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 弟 客師

translations.literal: Younger brother: Keshe.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Keshe.

sentences.zh: 弟客師，右武衛將軍，累戰功封丹陽郡公。

translations.literal: The younger brother Keshe was General of the Right Martial Guard; through repeated battle merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Keshe served as general of the Right Martial Guard and, through repeated battle honors, was enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 致仕，居昆明池南。

translations.literal: He retired from office and dwelt south of Kunming Pond.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and lived south of Kunming Pond.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，喜馳獵，雖老猶未衰。

translations.literal: Skilled in riding and archery, he delighted in galloping hunts; though old he had not yet declined.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in riding and archery, he loved the chase, and even in old age his vigor had not faded.

sentences.zh: 自京南屬山，西際澧水，鳥鵲皆識之，每出，從之翔噪，人謂之「鳥賊」。

translations.literal: From the mountains south of the capital west to the Li River, birds and magpies all knew him; whenever he went out they followed him flying and clamoring—people called him the "Bird Bandit."
translations.idiomatic: From the hills south of the capital west to the Li River, birds and magpies knew him. Whenever he went out they followed him, wheeling and crying, and people called him the "Bird Bandit."

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十，贈幽州都督。

translations.literal: He died at ninety; posthumously made Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety and was posthumously named area commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 孫 令問

translations.literal: Grandson: Lingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Lingwen.

sentences.zh: 五代孫 彥芳

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant: Yanfang.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant: Yanfang.

sentences.zh: 靖五代孫彥芳，大和中，為鳳翔司錄參軍。

translations.literal: Jing's fifth-generation descendant Yanfang, in the Dahe reign, served as Registrar of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's fifth-generation descendant Yanfang served as registrar of Fengxiang during the Dahe era.

sentences.zh: 家故藏高祖、太宗賜靖詔書數函，上之。

translations.literal: His family had long kept several cases of edicts bestowed on Jing by Gaozu and Taizong; he presented them.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long kept several cases of edicts Gaozu and Taizong had bestowed on Jing, and he presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 一曰：「兵事節度皆付公，吾不從中治也。」

translations.literal: One read: "All military affairs and command are entrusted to you; I will not intervene from the center."
translations.idiomatic: One read, "All military affairs and command are entrusted to you. I will not intervene from the center."

sentences.zh: 一曰：「有晝夜視公疾大老嫗遣來，吾欲熟知公起居狀。」

translations.literal: Another read: "An old woman who watches your illness day and night has been sent—I wish to know your condition of daily living in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Another read, "I have sent an old woman to watch your illness day and night. I wish to know your daily condition in detail."

sentences.zh: 皆太宗手墨，它大略如此。

translations.literal: All were in Taizong's own hand; the others were broadly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: All were in Taizong's own hand; the others were much the same.

sentences.zh: 文宗愛之不廢手。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved them and could not put them down.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong loved them and could not put them down.

sentences.zh: 其舊物有佩筆，以木為管弢，刻金其上，別為環以限其間，筆尚可用也。

translations.literal: Among his old objects was a belt pen: a wooden sheath-case with gold carved on it, a separate ring to mark the interval—the pen could still be used.
translations.idiomatic: Among his relics was a belt pen in a wooden sheath with gold inlay and a separate ring to mark its place—the pen still worked.

sentences.zh: 靖破蕭銑時，所賜於闐玉帶十三胯，七方六刓，胯各附環，以金固之，所以佩物者。

translations.literal: When Jing defeated Xiao Xun he was given a Khotan jade belt of thirteen plaques—seven square and six round—each plaque with an attached ring, secured with gold: the objects worn on the belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing defeated Xiao Xun he received a Khotan jade belt of thirteen plaques—seven square and six round—each with a ring, set in gold: the fittings of his belt.

sentences.zh: 又有火鑒、大觿、算囊等物，常佩於帶者。

translations.literal: There were also a fire-striker, a large girdle pick, an abacus pouch, and other objects regularly worn on the belt.
translations.idiomatic: There were also a fire-striker, a large belt pick, an abacus pouch, and other objects he habitually wore on his belt.

sentences.zh: 天子悉留禁中。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven kept them all in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept them all in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 又敕摸詔本，還賜彥芳，並束帛衣服。

translations.literal: He also ordered copies made of the edicts and returned to Yanfang, together with bolts of silk and garments.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered copies of the edicts made and returned to Yanfang, together with bolts of silk and garments.

sentences.zh: 權德輿嘗讀太宗手詔，至流涕曰：「君臣之際乃爾邪！」

translations.literal: Quan Deyu once read Taizong's handwritten edicts and, weeping, said: "Can relations between ruler and minister truly be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu once read Taizong's handwritten edicts and wept, saying, "Can relations between ruler and minister truly be like this!"

sentences.zh: 李勣，字懋功，曹州離狐人。

translations.literal: Li Ji, styled Maogong, was a man of Lihu in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, whose style name was Maogong, came from Lihu in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 本姓徐氏，客衛南。

translations.literal: His original surname was Xu; he was a guest-retainer in Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Xu; his family had been guest-retainers in Weinan.

sentences.zh: 家富，多僮僕，積粟常數千鐘。

translations.literal: The family was wealthy, with many servants; stored grain often ran to several thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy, with many servants and grain stores often running to several thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 與其父蓋皆喜施貸，所周給無親疏之間。

translations.literal: He and his father Gai both delighted in giving and lending; those they aided made no distinction of near or distant kin.
translations.idiomatic: He and his father Gai both delighted in giving and lending, helping near and distant kin alike.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，韋城翟讓為盜，勣年十七，往從之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui Daye reign Zhai Rang of Weicheng became a bandit; Ji was seventeen and went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui Daye era, Zhai Rang of Weicheng turned bandit. Ji was seventeen and joined him.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「公鄉壤不宜自剽殘，宋、鄭商旅之會，禦河在中，舟艦相屬，往邀取之，可以自資。」

translations.literal: He urged: "Your native district is not fit for self-plunder; Song and Zheng are meeting places of merchants and travelers—the Imperial River runs through them and boats and ships follow one another—go intercept them and you can supply yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: He urged, "Your home ground is no place for plundering your own people. Song and Zheng are hubs of merchant traffic—the Imperial River runs between them and boats pass in endless train. Intercept them and you can supply yourselves."

sentences.zh: 讓然之。

translations.literal: Rang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Rang agreed.

sentences.zh: 劫公私船取財，繇是兵大振。

translations.literal: They robbed public and private boats for wealth; thereby the army swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They robbed merchant and official vessels for plunder, and the army swelled greatly.

sentences.zh: 李密亡命雍丘，勣與浚儀王伯當共說讓，推密為主。

translations.literal: Li Mi was a fugitive at Yongqiu; Ji and Wang Bodang of Junyi together urged Rang to make Mi leader.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was in hiding at Yongqiu. Ji and Wang Bodang of Junyi together urged Rang to make Mi their leader.

sentences.zh: 以奇計破王世充。

translations.literal: With a stratagem he defeated Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: With a stratagem he defeated Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 密署勣右武候大將軍、東海郡公。

translations.literal: Mi appointed Ji Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mi appointed Ji grand general of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河南、山東大水，隋帝令饑人就食黎陽倉，吏不時發，死者日數萬。

translations.literal: At that time Henan and Shandong suffered great floods; the Sui emperor ordered the hungry to go eat at the Liyang granary, but officials did not issue grain in time and tens of thousands died daily.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Shandong were then ravaged by flood. The Sui emperor ordered the hungry to the Liyang granary, but officials failed to issue grain in time, and tens of thousands died each day.

sentences.zh: 勣說密曰：「天下之亂本於饑，今若取黎陽粟以募兵，大事濟矣。」

translations.literal: Ji urged Mi: "The root of the realm's disorder is hunger—if we now take the grain of Liyang to raise troops, the great enterprise will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Ji urged Mi, "The root of the realm's disorder is hunger. If we take the grain at Liyang to raise troops, the great enterprise will succeed."

sentences.zh: 密以麾下兵五千付勣，與郝孝德等濟河，襲黎陽，守之。

translations.literal: Mi gave Ji five thousand troops under his command; with Hao Xiaode and others they crossed the river, raided Liyang, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi gave Ji five thousand men. With Hao Xiaode and others he crossed the river, seized Liyang, and held it.

sentences.zh: 開倉縱食，旬日，勝兵至二十萬。

translations.literal: They opened the granary and released grain; within ten days fit soldiers reached two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the granaries. Within ten days their effective force reached two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及擁兵北上，密使勣守倉，周掘塹以自環。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji led troops north; Mi had Ji guard the granary and dig trenches all around for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji marched north with his army. Mi left Ji to guard the granary and had trenches dug all around.

sentences.zh: 化及攻之，勣為地道出鬥，化及敗，引去。

translations.literal: Huaji attacked; Ji made a tunnel to sally out and fight; Huaji was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji attacked. Ji tunneled out to fight, defeated him, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，密歸朝廷，其地東屬海，南至江，西直汝，北抵魏郡，勣統之，未有所屬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude Mi submitted to the court; his territory east reached the sea, south to the Yangzi, west to Ru, north to Weijun—Ji commanded it but it had not yet been assigned.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2, Mi submitted to the Tang. His territory ran east to the sea, south to the Yangzi, west to Ru, and north to Weijun. Ji still commanded it, but it had not yet been assigned to anyone.

sentences.zh: 謂長史郭孝恪曰：「人眾土宇，皆魏公有也。

translations.literal: He told Chief Administrator Guo Xiaoke: "The people and the territory all belong to the Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He told chief administrator Guo Xiaoke, "The people and the territory all belong to the Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 吾若獻之，是利主之敗為己功，吾所羞也。」

translations.literal: If I present them myself, that is to profit from my lord's defeat for my own merit—what I would be ashamed to do."
translations.idiomatic: If I presented them myself, I would be profiting from my lord's defeat—that is what I would be ashamed to do."

sentences.zh: 乃錄郡縣戶口以啟密，請自上之。

translations.literal: He then recorded the household registers of commanderies and counties and reported to Mi, asking that Mi present them himself.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded the commandery and county household registers and reported to Mi, asking Mi to present them himself.

sentences.zh: 使至，高祖訝無表，使者以意聞。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived Gaozu was surprised there was no memorial; the envoy conveyed the intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, Gaozu was surprised there was no memorial. The envoy explained Ji's intent.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「純臣也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "A pure minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "A loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 詔授黎州總管，封萊國公。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Area Commander of Lizhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him area commander of Lizhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lai.

sentences.zh: 賜姓，附宗正屬籍，徙封曹，給田五十頃，甲第一區。

translations.literal: He was granted the imperial surname, attached to the clan registry under the Director of Imperial Clans, transferred in enfeoffment to Cao, given fifty qing of fields and one first-rank residence.
translations.idiomatic: He received the imperial surname, was entered on the clan registry, transferred his enfeoffment to Cao, and received fifty qing of land and a first-rank residence.

sentences.zh: 封蓋濟陰王，固辭，改舒國公。

translations.literal: Gai was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyin but firmly declined; he was changed to Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gai was offered the title Prince of Jiyin but firmly declined and was made Duke of Shu instead.

sentences.zh: 詔勣總河南、山東兵以拒王世充。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ji to command the troops of Henan and Shandong to resist Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ji to command Henan and Shandong troops against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 及密以謀反誅，帝遣使示密反狀。

translations.literal: When Mi was executed for plotting rebellion, the emperor sent an envoy to show Ji the evidence of Mi's treason.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was executed for treason, the emperor sent an envoy to show Ji the evidence.

sentences.zh: 勣請收葬，詔從之。

translations.literal: Ji asked to gather and bury the body; an edict consented.
translations.idiomatic: Ji asked to bury Mi properly, and the edict consented.

sentences.zh: 勣為密服縗絰，葬訖乃釋。

translations.literal: Ji wore mourning hemp for Mi and only laid it aside after the burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wore full mourning for Mi and only laid it aside after the burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 俄為竇建德所陷，質其父，使復守黎陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was captured by Dou Jiande, who took his father hostage and made him guard Liyang again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dou Jiande captured him, took his father hostage, and made him guard Liyang again.

sentences.zh: 三年，自拔來歸。

translations.literal: In the third year he broke free and came back in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he broke free and returned to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 從秦王伐東都，戰有功。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in the campaign against the Eastern Capital and fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin against the Eastern Capital and distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 東略地至虎牢，降鄭州司兵沈悅。

translations.literal: Advancing east he seized territory to Hulao and received the surrender of Shen Yue, Registrar of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing east he reached Hulao and received the surrender of Shen Yue, registrar of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 平建德，俘世充，乃振旅還，秦王為上將，勣為下將，皆服金甲，乘戎輅，告捷於廟。

translations.literal: Jiande was pacified and Shichong captured; they then led the army back in triumph—the Prince of Qin as upper commander, Ji as lower commander—both in golden armor, riding war chariots, reporting victory at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Jiande and capturing Shichong, they led the army home in triumph. The Prince of Qin was upper commander and Ji lower commander; both wore golden armor, rode war chariots, and reported victory at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 蓋亦自洺州與裴矩入朝，詔復其官。

translations.literal: Gai also came to court from Mingzhou with Pei Ju; an edict restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: Gai also came to court from Mingzhou with Pei Ju, and an edict restored his office.

sentences.zh: 又從破劉黑闥、徐圓朗，累遷左監門大將軍。

translations.literal: He again followed in defeating Liu Heita and Xu Yuanlang and was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of the Left Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed campaigns that defeated Liu Heita and Xu Yuanlang and rose to grand general of the Left Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 圓朗復反，詔勣為河南大總管，討平之。

translations.literal: Yuanlang rebelled again; an edict made Ji Grand Area Commander of Henan and he pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang rebelled again. Ji was made grand area commander of Henan and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭討輔公祏也，遣勣以步卒一萬度淮，拔壽陽，攻江西賊壁，馮惠亮、陳正通相次潰，公祏平。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiaogong of Zhao attacked Fu Gongshi he sent Ji with ten thousand foot soldiers across the Huai, took Shouyang, assaulted the rebel strongholds west of the river; Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong collapsed in succession and Gongshi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiaogong of Zhao attacked Fu Gongshi, he sent Ji with ten thousand foot soldiers across the Huai. Ji took Shouyang, stormed the rebel camps west of the river, and after Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong collapsed in turn, Gongshi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，拜并州都督，賜實封九百戶。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Ji was appointed Area Commander of Bingzhou and granted nine hundred taxable households in substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Ji became area commander of Bingzhou with nine hundred taxable households in substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，為通漠道行軍總管，出雲中，與突厥戰，走之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was made Campaign Commander of the Tongmo Circuit, marched out from Yunzhong, fought the Turks, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 he was made campaign commander on the Tongmo circuit, marched from Yunzhong, fought the Turks, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 引兵與李靖合。

translations.literal: He led troops to join Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He brought his troops to join Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「頡利若度磧，保於九姓，果不可得，我若約齎薄之，不戰縛虜矣。」

translations.literal: He then said: "If Jieli crosses the desert and shelters among the Nine Surnames, he truly cannot be taken—but if we travel light with scant supplies, we can bind the captive without battle."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If Jieli crosses the desert and shelters among the Nine Surnames, he cannot be taken—but if we travel light with little baggage, we can take him without a battle."

sentences.zh: 靖大喜，以與己合，於是意決。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly pleased that this agreed with his own view and so his resolve was set.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was delighted that this matched his own thinking, and his mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 靖率眾夜發，勣勒兵從之。

translations.literal: Jing led the host forward by night; Ji drove the troops in his wake.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led the army out by night; Ji drove the troops after him.

sentences.zh: 頡利欲走磧，勣前屯磧口，不得度，由是酋長率部落五萬降於勣。

translations.literal: Jieli wished to flee across the desert; Ji advanced and encamped at the desert pass so he could not cross; thereby chieftains led fifty thousand of their tribes to surrender to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli tried to flee across the desert. Ji camped at the pass and blocked him. Fifty thousand tribesmen then surrendered to Ji.

sentences.zh: 詔拜光祿大夫，行并州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Chief Administrator of the Bingzhou Superior Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting chief administrator of the Bingzhou superior command.

sentences.zh: 父喪解，奪哀還官，徙封英，治并州十六年，以威肅聞。

translations.literal: He left office for his father's mourning, then was recalled from mourning to his post; his enfeoffment was moved to Ying; he governed Bingzhou sixteen years and was known for awe-inspiring discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning, was recalled before mourning ended, was transferred to the Ying enfeoffment, governed Bingzhou for sixteen years, and was known for stern discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「煬帝不擇人守邊，勞中國築長城以備虜。

translations.literal: The emperor once said: "Emperor Yang did not choose men to guard the frontier and exhausted China building the Long Wall to guard against barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "Emperor Yang did not choose the right men to guard the frontier and exhausted China building the Long Wall against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 今我用勣守並，突厥不敢南，賢長城遠矣！」

translations.literal: Now I use Ji to guard Bing and the Turks dare not come south—how much better than a mere Long Wall!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I use Ji to guard Bingzhou, and the Turks dare not come south—far better than any wall!"

sentences.zh: 召為兵部尚書，未至，會薛延陀子大度設以八萬騎侵李思摩。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of War but had not yet arrived when the son of the Xueyantuo khan, Dadushe, invaded Li Simo with eighty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of War but had not yet arrived when Dadushe, son of the Xueyantuo khan, invaded Li Simo with eighty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 詔勣為朔方道行軍總管，將輕騎六千，擊度設青山，斬名王一，俘口五萬。

translations.literal: An edict made Ji Campaign Commander of the Shuofang Circuit; he led six thousand light cavalry, struck Dadushe at Qingshan, beheaded one royal prince, and captured fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Ji campaign commander on the Shuofang circuit. He led six thousand light cavalry, struck Dadushe at Qingshan, killed a royal prince, and took fifty thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以功封一子為縣公。

translations.literal: For merit one son was enfeoffed as Duke of a county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service one son was enfeoffed as a county duke.

sentences.zh: 晉王為皇太子，授詹事，兼左衛率，俄同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Ji was made Chamberlain and concurrently Left Guard Commander; soon he was made coequal with the Three Departments at the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Ji was made chamberlain and concurrently commander of the Left Guard; soon he joined the chief ministers at the third rank.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾兒方位東宮，公舊長史，以宮事相委，勿以資屈為嫌也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My son is now in the Eastern Palace; you were his former chief administrator—entrust the palace affairs to you; do not take lower rank as a grievance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My son is now in the Eastern Palace. You were his former chief administrator—I entrust palace affairs to you. Do not take lower rank as an insult."

sentences.zh: 後帝自將征高麗，以勣為遼東道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor personally led a campaign against Goguryeo, Ji was made Grand Campaign Commander of the Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor led the campaign against Goguryeo in person, Ji was made grand campaign commander on the Liaodong circuit.

sentences.zh: 破蓋牟、遼東、白崖等城，從戰駐蹕山，功多，封一子為郡公。

translations.literal: He captured Gaimou, Liaodong, Baiya, and other cities; followed in the campaign at Zhujianshan with many achievements; one son was enfeoffed as Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He took Gaimou, Liaodong, Baiya, and other cities, fought at Zhujianshan with great credit, and one son was enfeoffed as a commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 延陀部落亂，詔將二百騎發突厥兵討之，大戰烏德鞬山，破之，降其首領梯真達幹，而可汁咄摩支遁入荒穀，磧北遂定。

translations.literal: When the Yanluo tribes rebelled, an edict ordered him to lead two hundred horsemen to muster Turkic troops and suppress them; at Wudejian Mountain he fought a great battle, broke them, and received the surrender of their chieftain Tizhen Dagan, while Khan Tudu Mozhi fled into wild valleys and the north of the desert was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yanluo tribes rebelled, he led two hundred horsemen to raise Turkic allies and crushed them at Wudejian Mountain. Their chieftain Tizhen Dagan surrendered; Khan Tudu Mozhi fled into the wilds, and the northern desert was settled.

sentences.zh: 改太常卿，仍同中書門下三品，復為詹事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, still coequal with the chief ministers at the third rank, and again made Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, remained a chief minister at the third rank, and was again made chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 勣既忠力，帝謂可托大事。

translations.literal: Ji was loyal and forceful; the emperor judged that great affairs could be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was loyal and capable; the emperor believed great affairs could be entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗暴疾，毉曰：「用須灰可治。」

translations.literal: He once fell gravely ill; the physician said: "Ash is needed to treat it."
translations.idiomatic: He once fell gravely ill. The physician said ash was needed for the cure."

sentences.zh: 帝乃自翦須以和藥。

translations.literal: The emperor then cut his own beard to mix into the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cut his own beard to mix into the medicine.

sentences.zh: 及愈，入謝，頓首流血。

translations.literal: When he recovered he came to give thanks and kowtowed until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered he came to give thanks and kowtowed until his forehead bled.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾為社稷計，何謝為！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I did it for the altars of state—why thank me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I did it for the realm—why thank me?"

sentences.zh: 後留宴，顧曰：「朕思屬幼孤，無易公者。

translations.literal: Later he kept him at a banquet and said, looking at him: "I think of entrusting my young orphan to you—there is no one I would change for you.
translations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet he said, "I mean to entrust my young heir to you—there is no one I would prefer.

sentences.zh: 公昔不遺李密，豈負朕哉？」

translations.literal: You did not abandon Li Mi in the past—would you fail me?"
translations.idiomatic: You did not abandon Li Mi—would you fail me?"

sentences.zh: 勣感涕，因齧指流血。

translations.literal: Ji was moved to tears and bit his finger until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wept and bit his finger until it bled.

sentences.zh: 俄大醉，帝親解衣覆之。

translations.literal: Soon he was deeply drunk and the emperor personally removed his own robe to cover him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was deeply drunk, and the emperor removed his own robe to cover him.

sentences.zh: 帝疾，謂太子曰：「爾於勣無恩，今以事出之，我死，宜即授以僕射，彼必致死力矣！」

translations.literal: When the emperor was ill he told the crown prince: "You have shown Ji no favor; now send him away on some mission—when I die, promptly appoint him Vice Premier; he is sure to exert himself to the death!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill he told the crown prince, "You have shown Ji no favor. Send him away on some mission now. When I die, appoint him vice premier at once—he will serve you to the death!"

sentences.zh: 乃授疊州都督。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Area Commander of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed area commander of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，召授檢校洛州刺史、洛陽宮留守，進開府儀同三司、同中書門下，參掌機密，遂為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Ji was summoned and appointed Acting Governor of Luozhou and Keeper of the Luoyang Palace, advanced to Opening Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and coequal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, sharing in confidential affairs, and then made Left Vice Premier.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Ji was summoned as acting governor of Luozhou and keeper of the Luoyang palace, promoted to opening office with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies and coequal with the chief ministers, given a share in confidential affairs, and made left vice premier.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，求解僕射，聽之，仍以開府儀同三司知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he asked to resign the vice premiership and was permitted; he still held Opening Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 he asked to resign as vice premier and was allowed to do so, but retained opening office rank and continued to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，冊進司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was advanced to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 始太宗時，勣已畫象淩煙閣，至是，帝復命圖其形，自序之。

translations.literal: Already in Taizong's time Ji's portrait had been painted in the Lingyan Pavilion; now the emperor again ordered his likeness painted and wrote the inscription himself.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had already placed Ji's portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion; now the emperor ordered it painted again and wrote the inscription himself.

sentences.zh: 又詔得乘小馬出入東、西台，卑官日一人迎送。

translations.literal: An edict also allowed him to ride a small horse in and out of the eastern and western offices, with one low-ranking official each day to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also allowed him to ride a pony in and out of the eastern and western offices, with one low official each day to escort him.

sentences.zh: 帝欲立武昭儀為皇后，畏大臣異議，未決。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Consort Wu Zhaoyi empress but feared dissent among the great ministers and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Consort Wu empress but feared opposition from the great ministers and had not decided.

sentences.zh: 李義府、許敬宗又請廢王皇后。

translations.literal: Li Yifu and Xu Jingzong also asked to depose Queen Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu and Xu Jingzong also urged deposing Queen Wang.

sentences.zh: 帝召勣與長孫無忌、于志甯、褚遂良計之，勣稱疾不至。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Ji together with Zhangsun Wuji, Yu Zhining, and Chu Suiliang to deliberate; Ji claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Ji, Zhangsun Wuji, Yu Zhining, and Chu Suiliang to deliberate; Ji claimed illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「皇后無子。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The queen has no son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The queen has no son.

sentences.zh: 罪莫大於絕嗣，將廢之。」

translations.literal: No crime is greater than ending the succession—she will be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: No fault is greater than leaving the line without an heir. She will be deposed."

sentences.zh: 遂良等持不可，志甯顧望不對。

translations.literal: Suiliang and others held that it could not be done; Zhining looked about and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang and others objected; Zhining looked away and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝后密訪勣，曰：「將立昭儀，而顧命之臣皆以為不可，今止矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor and empress secretly consulted Ji, saying: "I mean to establish Zhaoyi, but the ministers entrusted at my deathbed all say it cannot be—now it stops!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress secretly consulted Ji: "I mean to make Zhaoyi empress, but the ministers I entrusted at my deathbed all oppose it—so it stops!"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「此陛下家事，無須問外人。」

translations.literal: He answered: "This is Your Majesty's family affair—there is no need to ask outsiders."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "This is Your Majesty's family affair. There is no need to ask outsiders."

sentences.zh: 帝意遂定，而王后廢。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent was then fixed, and Queen Wang was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up, and Queen Wang was deposed.

sentences.zh: 詔勣、志寧奉冊立武氏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ji and Zhining to present the investiture documents establishing the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ji and Zhining to present the documents investing Lady Wu as empress.

sentences.zh: 帝東封泰山，為封禪大使。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the eastern feng and shan rites at Mount Tai, Ji was made ambassador for the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the feng and shan rites at Mount Tai, Ji was made ambassador for the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 嘗墜馬傷足，帝以所乘馬賜之。

translations.literal: He once fell from a horse and injured his foot; the emperor gave him the horse he had been riding.
translations.idiomatic: He once fell from a horse and injured his foot; the emperor gave him the horse he had been riding.

sentences.zh: 高麗莫離支男生為其弟所逐，遣子乞師。

translations.literal: The Goguryeo Molich Zhi Nan-sheng was driven out by his younger brother and sent his son to beg for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo's Molich Zhi Nan-sheng was driven out by his younger brother and sent his son to beg for aid.

sentences.zh: 詔勣為遼東道行軍大總管，率兵二萬討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Ji Grand Campaign Commander of the Liaodong Circuit, leading twenty thousand troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Ji grand campaign commander on the Liaodong circuit with twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 破其國，執高藏、男建等，裂其地州縣之。

translations.literal: He broke their state, seized Gao Zang, Nan Jian, and others, and carved up their territory into prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He broke their state, seized Gao Zang and Nan Jian, and carved their territory into prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 詔勣獻俘昭陵，明先帝意，具軍容告於廟。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ji to present captives at Zhaoling, explain the late emperor's intent, and report in full military array at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ji to present captives at Zhaoling, explain the late emperor's intent, and report in full military array at the temple.

sentences.zh: 進位太子太師，增食千一百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and his food allotment increased by eleven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand preceptor of the crown prince and his food allotment increased by eleven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 總章二年，卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang he died at eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Zongzhang 2 he died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「勣奉上忠，事親孝，曆三朝未嘗有過，性廉慎，不立產業。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ji was loyal in serving his superiors and filial in serving his kin; through three reigns he never had a fault; by nature he was incorrupt and cautious and established no estates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ji was loyal to his superiors and filial to his kin. Through three reigns he never erred. He was incorrupt and cautious and built no estates.

sentences.zh: 今亡，當無贏貲。

translations.literal: Now that he is gone, there should be no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is gone, he should leave no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 有司其厚賵恤之。」

translations.literal: Let the authorities richly compensate and comfort the family."
translations.idiomatic: Let the authorities give a generous funeral grant."

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept.

sentences.zh: 舉哀光順門，七日不視朝。

translations.literal: Mourning was raised at Guangshun Gate; for seven days he did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning was raised at Guangshun Gate, and for seven days the emperor did not hold court.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、揚州大都督，諡貞武。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Superior Area Commander of Yangzhou; posthumous title Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand preceptor and superior area commander of Yangzhou, with the posthumous title Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 給秘器，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Secret burial vessels were granted and he was buried beside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Secret burial vessels were granted and he was buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 起塚象陰、鐵、烏德鞬山，以旌功烈。

translations.literal: His tomb was built to resemble the Yin Mountains, Tieshan, and Wudejian Mountain to honor his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His tomb was built to resemble the Yin Mountains, Tieshan, and Wudejian Mountain to honor his achievements.

sentences.zh: 葬日，帝與皇太子幸未央古城，哭送，百官送古城西北。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the emperor and crown prince went to the old city of Weiyang to weep and send him off; the hundred officials escorted him to the northwest of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day the emperor and crown prince went to the old Weiyang city to weep and send him off; officials escorted the procession northwest of the old city.

sentences.zh: 初，勣拔黎陽倉，就食者眾，高季輔、杜正倫往客焉，及平虎牢，獲戴胄，鹹引見臥內，推禮之，後皆為名臣，世以勣知人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji opened the Liyang granary, many came to eat; Gao Jifu and Du Zhenglun lodged with him as guests; when Hulao was pacified he obtained Dai Zhou and received them in his inner quarters with courtesy—all later became famous ministers; the age praised Ji for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji opened the Liyang granary, Gao Jifu and Du Zhenglun were among those who came to eat. After Hulao fell he obtained Dai Zhou. He received them all in his inner quarters with honor; each later became a famous minister, and the age praised Ji for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 平洛陽，得單雄信，故人也。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified he captured Shan Xiongxin, an old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was pacified he captured Shan Xiongxin, an old friend.

sentences.zh: 表其材武，且言：「若貸死，必有以報，請納官爵以贖。」

translations.literal: He memorialized Xiongxin's martial talent and moreover said: "If his life is spared, he is sure to repay—please let me yield my office and rank to redeem him."
