translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Xiongxin's martial talent and said, "If his life is spared he will surely repay the favor—let me yield my office and rank to redeem him."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乃號慟，割股肉啗之曰：「生死永訣，此肉同歸於土！」

translations.literal: He then wailed, cut flesh from his thigh, and fed it to him, saying: "We part forever in life and death—this flesh returns with you to the earth!
translations.idiomatic: He wailed, cut flesh from his thigh, and fed it to him, saying, "We part forever—this flesh goes with you to the earth!

sentences.zh: 為收養其子焉。

translations.literal: He then took in and raised his son.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his son.

sentences.zh: 性友愛，其姊病，嘗自為粥而燎其須。

translations.literal: By nature he was affectionate toward kin; when his elder sister was ill he once made porridge himself and singed his beard.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply affectionate. When his elder sister fell ill he made porridge himself and singed his beard.

sentences.zh: 姊戒止。

translations.literal: His sister admonished him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: His sister told him to stop.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「姊多疾，而勣且老，雖欲數進粥，尚幾何？」

translations.literal: He answered: "Elder sister, you are often ill and I am already old—even if I wished to bring you porridge often, how much time is left?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Sister, you are often ill and I am already old. Even if I brought you porridge often, how much time is left?"

sentences.zh: 其用兵多籌算，料敵應變，皆契事機。

translations.literal: In using troops he relied much on calculation; in sizing up the enemy and responding to change he always matched the moment.
translations.idiomatic: In war he relied on calculation; in reading the enemy and adapting he always matched the moment.

sentences.zh: 聞人善，抵掌嗟歎。

translations.literal: When he heard of others' excellence he would clap his hands and sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of someone's excellence he clapped his hands and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 及戰勝，必推功於下。

translations.literal: When victorious he always pushed merit down to his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he always gave the credit to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 得金帛，盡散之士卒，無私貯。

translations.literal: Gold and silk obtained he distributed entirely to the soldiers, keeping nothing in private store.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silk he distributed entirely to the soldiers, keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 然持法嚴，故人為之用。

translations.literal: Yet he held the law strictly, and therefore men served him willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he held the law strictly, and men served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 臨事選將，必訾相其奇厖福艾者遣之。

translations.literal: When choosing generals on campaign he always picked out those with strange features and the marks of fortune and long life to send.
translations.idiomatic: When choosing generals he always picked men with striking features and the marks of fortune and long life.

sentences.zh: 或問故，答曰：「薄命之人，不足與成功名。」

translations.literal: When asked why, he answered: "Men of thin fate are not fit to win achievement and fame."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Men of thin fate cannot win achievement and fame.

sentences.zh: 既沒，士皆為流涕。

translations.literal: After his death soldiers all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the soldiers all wept for him.

sentences.zh: 自屬疾，帝及皇太子賜藥即服，家欲呼毉巫，不許。

translations.literal: From the onset of illness the emperor and crown prince sent medicine which he took at once; when the household wished to call physicians and shamans he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he fell ill, the emperor and crown prince sent medicine which he took at once. When the household wished to call physicians he refused.

sentences.zh: 諸子固以藥進，輒曰：「我山東田夫耳，位三公，年逾八十，非命乎！

translations.literal: His sons pressed medicine on him; he would say: "I am but a farmer from east of the mountains who rose to the Three Excellencies and passed eighty—is that not fate!
translations.idiomatic: When his sons pressed medicine on him he said, "I am but a farmer from Shandong who rose to the Three Excellencies and passed eighty—is that not fate?

sentences.zh: 生死系天，寧就毉求活耶？」

translations.literal: Life and death depend on Heaven—why seek life from physicians?"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death depend on Heaven. Why seek life from physicians?

sentences.zh: 弟弼，始為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bi had first been Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bi had first been governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 以勣疾，召為司衛卿，使省視。

translations.literal: Because of Ji's illness he was summoned as Director of the Palace Guards to oversee care.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Ji's illness he was summoned as director of the palace guards to oversee his care.

sentences.zh: 忽語曰：「我似少愈，可置酒相樂。」

translations.literal: Suddenly he said: "I seem a little better—set out wine for a gathering."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he said, "I seem a little better. Set out wine for a gathering."

sentences.zh: 於是奏樂宴飲，列子孫於下。

translations.literal: Music was played and they feasted, with sons and grandsons arrayed below.
translations.idiomatic: Music was played and they feasted, with sons and grandsons below.

sentences.zh: 將罷，謂弼曰：「我即死，欲有言，恐悲哭不得盡，故一訣耳！

translations.literal: As it was about to end he told Bi: "I am about to die and wish to speak, but I fear grief will prevent me from finishing—so this one farewell!
translations.idiomatic: As the feast ended he told Bi, "I am about to die and have words to leave, but I fear weeping will cut them short—so this one farewell!

sentences.zh: 我見房玄齡、杜如晦、高季輔皆辛苦立門戶，亦望詒後，悉為不肖子敗之。

translations.literal: I have seen Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Gao Jifu all toil to raise their houses and hope to leave something to posterity, yet all were ruined by unworthy sons.
translations.idiomatic: I saw Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Gao Jifu toil to raise their houses and hope to benefit posterity, yet unworthy sons ruined them all.

sentences.zh: 我子孫今以付汝，汝可慎察，有不厲言行、交非類者，急榜殺以聞，毋令後人笑吾，猶吾笑房、杜也。

translations.literal: I now entrust my sons and grandsons to you—you must watch carefully; any whose conduct is not stern or who keeps bad company, quickly beat them to death and report it; do not let later men laugh at me as I laughed at Fang and Du.
translations.idiomatic: I entrust my sons and grandsons to you. Watch carefully. Any whose conduct is not stern or who keeps bad company—beat them to death at once and report it. Do not let later men laugh at me as I laughed at Fang and Du.

sentences.zh: 我死，布裝露車載柩，斂以常服，加朝服其中，儻死有知，庶著此奉見先帝。

translations.literal: When I die, carry the coffin in a plain cart with exposed bier, enshroud me in ordinary dress with court robes placed within—if the dead have awareness, perhaps in these I may meet the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, carry the coffin in a plain cart with exposed bier, dress me in ordinary clothes with court robes inside—if the dead have awareness, perhaps I may meet the late emperor thus.

sentences.zh: 明器惟作五六寓馬，下帳施幔，為皁頂白紗裙，中列十偶人，它不得以從。

translations.literal: Funerary figures only five or six clay horses; hang a canopy below the pall, black cap and white gauze skirt; arrange ten figurines within—nothing else may follow.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary figures: only five or six clay horses. Hang a canopy below the pall, black cap and white gauze skirt, ten figurines within—nothing else may follow.

sentences.zh: 眾妾願留養子者聽，餘出之。

translations.literal: Concubines who wish to remain to raise sons may do so; the rest are to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines who wish to stay and raise sons may do so; the rest must leave.

sentences.zh: 葬已，徙居我堂，善視小弱。

translations.literal: After burial move into my hall and care well for the young and weak.
translations.idiomatic: After burial move into my hall and care for the young and weak.

sentences.zh: 苟違我言，同戮屍矣！」

translations.literal: If you disobey my words, slaughter the corpse together!"
translations.idiomatic: If you disobey my words, you will share the corpse's fate!"

sentences.zh: 乃不復語。

translations.literal: He spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke no more.

sentences.zh: 弼等遵焉。

translations.literal: Bi and the others followed his instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and the others followed his instructions.

sentences.zh: 勣本二名，至高宗時，避太宗偏諱，故但名勣。

translations.literal: Ji originally bore two characters in his name; by Gaozong's time, to avoid the partial taboo on Taizong, he was called only Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji originally had two characters in his name; under Gaozong, to avoid Taizong's partial taboo, he was called only Ji.

sentences.zh: 後配享高宗廟廷。

translations.literal: Later he was granted a place in Gaozong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted a place in Gaozong's temple hall.

sentences.zh: 季弟感，年十五，有奇操。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Gan, at fifteen, had extraordinary resolve.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Gan, at fifteen, had extraordinary resolve.

sentences.zh: 李密敗，陷於世充。

translations.literal: When Li Mi was defeated he was trapped by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi was defeated he was trapped by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充令作書召勣，對曰：「兄尚節義，今巳事主，昆弟不能移也。」

translations.literal: Shichong ordered him to write summoning Ji; he replied: "Elder brother still holds to integrity and now serves a lord—we brothers cannot be moved."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong ordered him to write summoning Ji. He replied, "My brother still holds to integrity and now serves a lord. We brothers cannot be moved."

sentences.zh: 固不從，殺之。

translations.literal: He firmly refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 勣子震嗣，終桂州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji's son Zhen succeeded him and ended as Governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Zhen succeeded him and ended as governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 震子敬業、敬猷。

translations.literal: Zhen's sons Jingye and Jingyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's sons: Jingye and Jingyou.

sentences.zh: 孫 敬業

translations.literal: Grandson: Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Jingye.

sentences.zh: 敬業，少從勣征伐，有勇名。

translations.literal: Jingye, from youth following Ji in campaigns, had a reputation for valor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye, from youth following Ji in campaigns, had a reputation for valor.

sentences.zh: 曆太僕少卿，襲英國公，為眉州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, inherited the title Duke of Ying, and was made Governor of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the imperial stud, inherited the title Duke of Ying, and was made governor of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，坐贓，貶柳州司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng he was punished for corruption and demoted to Vice Magistrate of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sisheng he was punished for corruption and demoted to vice magistrate of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會給事中唐之奇貶括蒼令，詹事府司直杜求仁貶黝令，長安主簿駱賓王貶臨海丞，敬猷自盩厔令坐事免，俱客揚州，失職怏怏。

translations.literal: At that time Remonstrance Officer Tang Zhiqi was demoted to magistrate of Kuocang, Court Gentleman Du Qiuren to magistrate of You, Chief Clerk of the Heir Apparent's Household Luo Binwang to assistant magistrate of Linhai, Jingyou was dismissed from magistrate of Zhouzhi for an offense—all lodged in Yangzhou, discontented at losing office.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officer Tang Zhiqi was demoted to Kuocang, court gentleman Du Qiuren to You, chief clerk Luo Binwang to Linhai, and Jingyou dismissed from Zhouzhi—all lodged in Yangzhou, bitter over lost office.

sentences.zh: 時武后既廢中宗，又立睿宗，實亦囚之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Wu had already deposed Zhongzong and installed Ruizong, who was in fact also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: By then Empress Wu had deposed Zhongzong and installed Ruizong, who was also a prisoner in fact.

sentences.zh: 諸武擅命，唐子孫誅戮，天下憤之。

translations.literal: The Wu clan acted by their own authority; Tang imperial descendants were slaughtered—the realm was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan acted by their own authority; Tang princes were slaughtered, and the realm was enraged.

sentences.zh: 敬業等乘人怨，謀起兵，先諭其党監察御史薛璋，求使江都。

translations.literal: Jingye and the others seized on popular resentment to plot rebellion; they first persuaded their comrade Investigative Censor Xue Zhang to seek assignment to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye and the others seized on popular resentment and plotted rebellion, first persuading their comrade investigative censor Xue Zhang to seek assignment to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 及至，令雍人韋超告州長史陳敬之反，璋乃收系之。

translations.literal: When he arrived he had a native of Yong, Wei Chao, report to the prefectural chief administrator Chen Jingzhi that Jingzhi had rebelled; Zhang then arrested and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he had a Yong native, Wei Chao, accuse prefectural chief administrator Chen Jingzhi of rebellion; Zhang arrested him.

sentences.zh: 敬業即矯制殺敬之，自稱州司馬，且言奉密詔募兵，討高州叛酋。

translations.literal: Jingye then forged an edict executing Jingzhi, styled himself prefectural Vice Magistrate, and said he was raising troops by secret edict to punish the rebel chieftain of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye forged an edict executing Jingzhi, styled himself prefectural vice magistrate, and claimed a secret order to raise troops against a Gaozhou rebel chieftain.

sentences.zh: 即開府庫，令參軍李宗臣釋系囚、役工數百人，授甲，斬錄事參軍孫處行以徇。

translations.literal: He opened the treasury, had staff officer Li Zongchen release imprisoned laborers and conscripts numbering several hundred, arm them, and behead Registrar Sun Chuxing as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the treasury, had staff officer Li Zongchen release hundreds of prisoners and laborers, arm them, and behead registrar Sun Chuxing as a warning.

sentences.zh: 乃開三府，一曰匡復府，二曰英公府，三曰揚州大都督府。

translations.literal: He then opened three offices: one called the Restoration Office, one the Duke of Ying Office, one the Yangzhou Superior Area Command Office.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened three offices: the Restoration Office, the Duke of Ying Office, and the Yangzhou Superior Command Office.

sentences.zh: 自稱匡復府上將，領揚州大都督，以子奇為左長史，求仁右長史，宗臣左司馬，璋右司馬，江都令韋知止為英公府長史，賓王為藝文令，前盩厔尉魏思溫為軍師。

translations.literal: He styled himself Supreme Commander of the Restoration Office and Superior Area Commander of Yangzhou; made Ziqi Left Chief Administrator, Qiuren Right Chief Administrator, Zongchen Left Vice Magistrate, Zhang Right Vice Magistrate, Jiangdu Magistrate Wei Zhizhi Chief Administrator of the Duke of Ying Office, Binwang Director of Literary Arts, and former Zhouzhi Wei Siwen Military Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself supreme commander of the Restoration Office and superior area commander of Yangzhou, made Ziqi left chief administrator, Qiuren right chief administrator, Zongchen left vice magistrate, Zhang right vice magistrate, Jiangdu magistrate Wei Zhizhi chief administrator of the Duke of Ying office, Binwang director of literary arts, and former Zhouzhi magistrate Wei Siwen military adviser.

sentences.zh: 旬日，兵十余萬。

translations.literal: Within ten days his troops exceeded a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days his army exceeded a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 傳檄州縣，疏武氏過惡，復廬陵王天子位。

translations.literal: He sent proclamations to prefectures and counties, listing the Wu clan's crimes, and restored Prince Luling to the Son of Heaven's throne.
translations.idiomatic: He sent proclamations to prefectures and counties denouncing the Wu clan and restoring Prince Luling to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又索狀類太子賢者奉之，詭眾曰：「賢實不死。」

translations.literal: He also sought someone resembling the deposed Crown Prince Xian to install, deceiving the masses by saying: "Xian in fact did not die.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought someone resembling the deposed Crown Prince Xian to install, telling the crowd, "Xian is not dead.

sentences.zh: 楚州司馬李崇福率所部三縣應之。

translations.literal: Chuzhou Vice Magistrate Li Chongfu led the three counties under him in response.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou vice magistrate Li Chongfu led his three counties in response.

sentences.zh: 武后遣左玉鈐衛大將軍李孝逸兵三十萬往擊之，削其祖父官爵，毀塚藏，除屬籍，赦揚、楚民脅從者。

translations.literal: Empress Wu sent Left Jade-Ornamented Guard General Li Xiaoyi with three hundred thousand troops to attack; stripped the offices and ranks of Jingye's grandfather, destroyed the tombs and stores, removed them from the clan registry, and pardoned the people of Yang and Chu who had followed under compulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent Left Jade-Ornamented Guard General Li Xiaoyi with three hundred thousand troops, stripped Jingye's grandfather of office and rank, destroyed the family tombs, removed them from the clan registry, and pardoned coerced followers in Yang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 購得敬業首，授官三品，賞帛五千；

translations.literal: A reward was posted for Jingye's head—office of the third rank and five thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: A reward was posted for Jingye's head: third-rank office and five thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 得之奇等首，官五品，帛三千。

translations.literal: for the heads of Ziqi and the others, office of the fifth rank and three thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: for Ziqi and the others' heads, fifth-rank office and three thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 敬業問計于思溫，對曰：「公既以太后幽縶天子，宜身自將兵直趨洛陽。

translations.literal: Jingye asked Siwen for counsel; he answered: "Your Lordship has charged that the empress dowager has imprisoned the Son of Heaven—you ought to lead the army yourself straight for Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye asked Siwen for counsel. He answered, "You say the empress dowager has imprisoned the emperor. Lead the army yourself straight for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 山東、韓、魏知公勤王，附者必眾，天下指日定矣！」

translations.literal: Shandong, Han, and Wei will know you march to rescue the throne; those who join will surely be many—the realm will be settled within days!"
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and the old heartlands will know you march to rescue the throne. Supporters will flock to you, and the realm will be settled within days!"

sentences.zh: 璋曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhang said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, "No.

sentences.zh: 金陵負江，其地足以為固。

translations.literal: Jinling lies against the Yangzi; its terrain is enough to make a stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling lies on the Yangzi; its terrain is strong enough for a base.

sentences.zh: 且王氣尚在，宜先並常、潤為霸基，然後鼓行而北。」

translations.literal: Moreover the royal aura still remains—you should first seize Chang and Run as a hegemonic foundation, then beat the drums and march north."
translations.idiomatic: The royal aura still lingers there. Seize Chang and Run as your base, then march north."

sentences.zh: 思溫曰：「鄭、汴、徐、亳士皆豪傑，不願武后居上，蒸麥為飯，以待我師。

translations.literal: Siwen said: "The gentry of Zheng, Bian, Xu, and Bo are all heroes who do not wish Empress Wu above them—they steam wheat for food awaiting our army.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen said, "The gentry of the central plains are heroes who reject Empress Wu. They steam wheat and await our army.

sentences.zh: 奈何欲守金陵，投死地乎？」

translations.literal: Why seek to hold Jinling and cast yourselves into a dead land?"
translations.idiomatic: Why hold Jinling and throw yourselves into a dead end?"

sentences.zh: 敬業不從。

translations.literal: Jingye would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye would not listen.

sentences.zh: 使敬猷屯淮陰，韋超屯都梁山，自引兵擊潤州，下之。

translations.literal: He sent Jingyou to encamp at Huaiyin and Wei Chao at Duliang Mountain; he himself led troops to attack Runzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jingyou to Huaiyin and Wei Chao to Duliang Mountain, then led the main force against Runzhou and took it.

sentences.zh: 署宗臣為刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Zongchen governor.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zongchen governor.

sentences.zh: 始回兵屯高郵，下阿溪。

translations.literal: Only then did he turn the army back to encamp at Gaoyou and take Axi.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned back to camp at Gaoyou and took Axi.

sentences.zh: 思溫歎曰：「兵忌分，今敬業不知掃地度淮，率山東士先襲東都，吾知無能為也！」

translations.literal: Siwen sighed: "Armies dread division—now Jingye does not sweep the ground and cross the Huai, leading Shandong men first to strike the eastern capital; I know he can accomplish nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Siwen sighed, "Armies dread division. Jingye will not cross the Huai and strike the eastern capital first—I know he will accomplish nothing!"

sentences.zh: 武后又使黑齒常之將江南兵為孝逸援，進擊，淮陰、都梁兵皆敗。

translations.literal: The empress also sent Heichi Changzhi to lead Jiangnan troops as reinforcements for Xiaoyi; advancing to attack, the Huaiyin and Duliang forces were both defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The empress also sent Heichi Changzhi with Jiangnan troops to reinforce Xiaoyi. Both Huaiyin and Duliang fell.

sentences.zh: 後軍總管蘇孝祥率奇兵五千夜度擊敬業，孝祥死，兵溺者過半，孝逸軍退守石樑。

translations.literal: Rear Army Commander Su Xiaoxiang led five thousand elite troops in a night crossing to strike Jingye; Xiaoxiang died and more than half the men drowned; Xiaoyi's army withdrew to defend Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Rear army commander Su Xiaoxiang led five thousand elite troops in a night attack. Xiaoxiang was killed and more than half drowned. Xiaoyi withdrew to Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 有鳥群噪敬業營上，監軍御史魏真宰曰：「賊其敗乎！

translations.literal: Flocks of birds clamored above Jingye's camp; Supervisory Censor Wei Zhenzai said: "The rebels are about to be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Birds clamored above Jingye's camp. Supervisory censor Wei Zhenzai said, "The rebels are about to break!

sentences.zh: 風順荻乾，火攻之利也。」

translations.literal: The wind favors us and the reeds are dry—the advantage lies in fire attack."
translations.idiomatic: The wind favors us and the reeds are dry—fire is the weapon to use."

sentences.zh: 固請戰，遂度溪擊之。

translations.literal: He pressed for battle and crossed the stream to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed for battle and crossed the stream to attack.

sentences.zh: 敬業置陣久，士疲，皆顧望不正列，孝逸乘風縱火逼其軍，軍稍卻。

translations.literal: Jingye had long been in formation; the men were weary and all looked about without holding their ranks straight; Xiaoyi rode the wind and loosed fire to press the army, which gradually fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye's men had stood in formation too long. They were weary and their ranks wavered. Xiaoyi used the wind to set fire to the reeds and press them back.

sentences.zh: 敬業麾精兵居前，弱者在後，陣亂不能制，乃敗，斬七千餘級。

translations.literal: Jingye waved elite troops to the front and weak men to the rear; the formation fell into disorder and could not be controlled; they were defeated and more than seven thousand were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye put elites in front and weak men behind, but the formation collapsed. They were routed; more than seven thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 敬業與敬猷、之奇、求仁、賓王輕騎遁江都，悉焚其圖籍，攜妻子奔潤州，潛蒜山下，將入海逃高麗，抵海陵，阻風遺山江中，其將王那相斬之，凡二十五首，傳東都，皆夷其家。

translations.literal: Jingye with Jingyou, Zhiqi, Qiuren, and Binwang fled on light horses to Jiangdu, burned all their maps and registers, took wives and children and ran to Runzhou, hid at Mount Suanshan, meant to flee by sea to Goguryeo, reached Hailing, was blocked by wind and stranded on a hill in the river; his officer Wang Naxiang beheaded him—twenty-five heads in all were sent to the eastern capital and all their families were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye, Jingyou, Zhiqi, Qiuren, and Binwang fled to Jiangdu, burned their records, took families to Runzhou, hid at Mount Suanshan, and meant to flee by sea to Goguryeo. At Hailing, wind blocked them. Officer Wang Naxiang beheaded Jingye. Twenty-five heads were sent to Luoyang, and all their families were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 中宗反正，詔還勣官封屬籍，葺完塋塚焉。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, an edict returned Ji's offices, enfeoffments, and clan registry and repaired the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored, an edict returned Ji's offices, enfeoffments, and clan registry and repaired the tombs.

sentences.zh: 初，敬業之叔思文為潤州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jingye's uncle Siwen had been Governor of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye's uncle Siwen had been governor of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬業兵起，以使間道聞，固守逾月。

translations.literal: When Jingye raised troops, word came by envoy on a secret route; he held firm for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingye rebelled, word came by secret envoy, and Siwen held the city for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 城陷，敬業責曰：「廬陵王繼天下，無罪見廢，今兵以義動，何過拒邪？

translations.literal: When the city fell Jingye reproached him: "Prince Luling succeeds the realm without crime yet was deposed—now our army moves in righteousness; what fault is there in resisting?
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Jingye reproached him: "Prince Luling was deposed without crime. Our army moves in righteousness—why resist?

sentences.zh: 若太后是助，宜即姓武。」

translations.literal: If you mean to aid the empress dowager, you ought to take the surname Wu at once."
translations.idiomatic: If you aid the empress dowager, take the surname Wu at once."

sentences.zh: 思溫等欲殺之，敬業不許。

translations.literal: Siwen and others wished to kill him; Jingye would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen and others wished to kill him, but Jingye refused.

sentences.zh: 及揚、楚平，乃獨免。

translations.literal: Only when Yang and Chu were pacified was he alone spared.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Yang and Chu were pacified was he alone spared.

sentences.zh: 後遂賜武姓，曆春官尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was granted the surname Wu and served as Minister of the Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted the surname Wu and served as Minister of the Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 或言本與敬業謀者，乃復徐氏，卒。

translations.literal: Some said he had originally plotted with Jingye; he was then restored to the surname Xu and died.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had plotted with Jingye from the start; he was restored to the surname Xu and died.

sentences.zh: 子欽憲，開元中，仕至國子祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Qinxian, in the Kaiyuan era, rose to Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinxian rose to director of the imperial university in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「唐興，其名將曰英、衛，皆擢罪亡之餘，遂能依乘風雲，勒功帝籍。

translations.literal: The commentator says: "When Tang rose, its famous generals were called Ying and Wei—both were chosen from among men who had fallen into guilt and exile, yet were able to ride the wind and clouds and inscribe merit on the imperial registers.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: "When Tang rose, its famous generals were Ying and Wei—men raised from guilt and exile who rode the wind and clouds and inscribed their merit on the imperial registers.

sentences.zh: 蓋君臣之際，固有以感之，獨推期運，非也。

translations.literal: Surely in the relations of ruler and minister there is something that moves them—it is not merely to push fate and fortune; that is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Surely something moves between ruler and minister—it is not merely fate. That view is wrong.

sentences.zh: 若靖闔門稱疾，畏遠權逼，功大而主不疑，雖古哲人，何以尚茲？

translations.literal: As for Jing shutting his gates and claiming illness, fearing and keeping distant from coercive power, with great achievement yet the ruler not doubting him—though ancient sages, how could they surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Jing shut his gates and claimed illness, kept away from coercive power, achieved greatly yet was not doubted—even ancient sages could hardly surpass this.

sentences.zh: 勣之節，見於黎陽，故太宗勤勤於托孤，誠有為也。

translations.literal: Ji's integrity appeared at Liyang; therefore Taizong earnestly entrusted him with the orphan—he truly had cause.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's integrity showed at Liyang; Taizong earnestly entrusted him with the orphan, and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 至以老臣輔少主，會房帷易奪，天子畏大臣，依違不專，委誠取決，惟議是聽。

translations.literal: Yet when an old minister assisted a young sovereign, the inner chambers changed hands, the Son of Heaven feared great ministers, wavered without resolve, entrusted his sincerity and took decisions, listening only to deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when an old minister assisted a young sovereign, the inner chambers changed hands, the emperor feared great ministers, wavered, and took counsel only from deliberation.

sentences.zh: 勣乃私己畏禍，從而導之，武氏奮而唐之宗屬幾殲焉。

translations.literal: Ji then feared calamity for himself, followed and guided it—the Wu clan rose and Tang imperial kin were nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Ji feared calamity for himself, followed and guided it—and the Wu clan rose while Tang imperial kin were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 及其孫，因民不忍，舉兵覆宗，至掘塚而暴其骨。

translations.literal: When his grandson, because the people could not bear it, raised troops and overturned the clan, they even dug up the tombs and exposed the bones.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson, because the people could not bear it, raised troops and ruined the clan; they dug up the tombs and exposed the bones.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，不幾一言而喪邦乎？

translations.literal: Alas, did he not nearly lose the state in a single word?
translations.idiomatic: Alas—did he not nearly lose the state in a single sentence?

sentences.zh: 惜其不通學術，昧夫臨大節不可奪之誼，反與許、李同科，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Pity that he did not master learning and did not understand that in great crises integrity cannot be wrested away—instead he shares the judgment of Xu and Li; should one not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Pity that he lacked learning and did not grasp that great crises test integrity—instead he shares Xu and Li's judgment. Let that be a warning!

sentences.zh: 世言靖精風角、鳥占、雲祲、孤虛之術，為善用兵。

translations.literal: The age says Jing mastered wind angles, bird augury, cloud signs, and guxu arts, and therefore used troops well.
translations.idiomatic: The age says Jing mastered wind angles, bird augury, cloud signs, and guxu arts, and therefore used troops well.

sentences.zh: 是不然，特以臨機果，料敵明，根于忠智而已。

translations.literal: That is not so—he was simply decisive in the moment, clear in sizing up the enemy, rooted in loyalty and wisdom, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: That is not so. He was decisive in the moment, clear about the enemy, rooted in loyalty and wisdom—that is all.

sentences.zh: 俗人傅著怪詭禨祥，皆不足信。

translations.literal: When common people spread strange omens and portents, none is fit to be believed.
translations.idiomatic: Strange omens spread by common people are not to be believed.

sentences.zh: 故列靖所設施如此。

translations.literal: Therefore Jing's measures are listed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Jing's measures are listed thus.
